name: Cordless Wet Dry Floor Cleaner
definition: A battery-powered upright household machine that dispenses cleaning liquid, agitates an approved hard floor and recovers dirty liquid into a separate tank in the same pass.
includedScope: Cordless upright floor washers with separate clean- and dirty-water paths
Models that collect documented wet and dry household debris while washing approved floors
excludedScope: Dry-only stick vacuums and mop-only appliances
Carpet extractors, wet-dry canister vacuums and robot floor cleaners
Unverified cleaning-solution, roller, filter, battery or charger compatibility
primaryApplications: Mixed wet and dry kitchen or dining-area messes
Edge and under-furniture cleaning where the exact model permits
headline: Cordless wet dry floor cleaner systems, tanks, rollers and buyer checks
description: This profile separates liquid delivery, brush action, recovery, tank capacity, runtime and maintenance so buyers can compare cordless floor washers without treating a vacuum-mop label as proof of surface fit or cleaning result.
metaDescription: Cordless wet dry floor cleaner guide covering tanks, rollers, runtime, models, standards, maintenance and buyer verification.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not electrical, battery, chemical, hygiene or surface-care advice. Confirm the exact regional model, manual, approved floor, solution, roller, filter, battery, charger and cleaning cycle before procurement or use.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.value: Cordless liquid-dispensing, agitating and recovery machine
keyFacts.evidence: Official product sources describe upright machines that wash and recover wet or dry soil in one pass.
keyFacts.scope: Named household floor washers; dry vacuums and extraction machines are excluded.

keyFacts.label: Surface boundary
keyFacts.value: Use only on surfaces approved for the exact model and solution
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer pages identify sealed hard-floor or model-specific multi-surface boundaries.
keyFacts.scope: Exact regional model, floor finish and solution.

keyFacts.label: Buyer verification
keyFacts.value: Match tanks, roller, filter, solution, battery and charger by part number
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed systems use product-specific consumables and energy systems.
keyFacts.scope: Exact serial family and sales market.

systemFlow.name: Energy and control
systemFlow.role: Supplies power and regulates pumps, roller and recovery motor.
systemFlow.evidence: Official pages describe cordless energy systems and model-specific controls.
systemFlow.scope: Exact battery, charger and operating mode.

systemFlow.name: Liquid delivery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Clean-water tank, solution dosing and pump
systemFlow.role: Feeds approved liquid to the floor-contact system.
systemFlow.evidence: Reviewed products identify clean-water tanks and controlled liquid delivery.
systemFlow.scope: Approved water, formula and dilution only.

systemFlow.name: Agitation and pickup
systemFlow.componentFamily: Roller or brush, scraper, suction path and head seals
systemFlow.role: Agitates soil and transfers liquid and debris into the recovery path.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources describe rotating floor-contact systems and wet-dry pickup.
systemFlow.scope: Named heads, rollers and approved debris.

systemFlow.name: Recovery and maintenance
systemFlow.componentFamily: Dirty-water tank, separator, filter and cleaning cycle
systemFlow.role: Stores recovered soil and defines post-use cleaning work.
systemFlow.evidence: Two-tank systems and cleaning or rinse cycles are documented by manufacturers.
systemFlow.scope: Exact service sequence; self-cleaning does not remove every manual task.

variants.name: Roller floor washer
variants.operatorRelationship: User pushes an upright head while liquid delivery and recovery operate
variants.spaceConstraints: Head width, recline angle, turning radius and dock footprint
variants.limitations: Roller count or edge claims do not prove site performance.
variants.evidence: Tineco, Shark and Kärcher publish upright roller-based formats.

variants.name: Steam-assisted floor washer
variants.taskScale: Sticky soil on approved hard floors
variants.operatorRelationship: User selects a documented wash or steam-assisted mode
variants.spaceConstraints: Cord or battery boundary, heat restrictions and cooldown
variants.limitations: Steam availability does not establish sanitization outside the stated method.
variants.evidence: BISSELL documents vacuum, wash and steam functions for model 3515.
variants.scope: Exact model, formula and surface instructions.

variants.name: Multi-function convertible system
variants.taskScale: Floor washing plus separately documented dry or handheld tasks
variants.operatorRelationship: User changes the configured cleaning body or head
variants.limitations: A multi-function kit is not one simultaneous cleaning mode.
variants.evidence: Philips documents AquaTrio wet-and-dry equipment and model-specific replacement assemblies.

performanceMetrics.name: Clean- and dirty-water capacity
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Potential route length before refill or emptying
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Nominal capacity differs from usable capacity and automatic stop point
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not compare one tank while ignoring the smaller limiting tank.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official specifications publish separate tank values for named models.

performanceMetrics.name: Runtime
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Available cordless operating time before recharge
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Mode, pump, roller load, battery state and surface affect runtime
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Maximum runtime is not verified cleaned area.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Tineco and Kärcher qualify runtime by model and operation.

performanceMetrics.name: Residual moisture
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Operational effect on dry-back time and slip exposure
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Floor finish, pass speed, scraper condition and liquid dose matter
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: A marketing dry-floor claim is not a matched test result.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers describe recovery and model-specific drying outcomes.

performanceMetrics.name: Edge and low-clearance access
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Reach near baseboards and under furniture
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Body thickness, recline rules, wheel position and tank orientation differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Photographs do not prove usable clearance or leak-free operation.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources describe edge cleaning and model-specific head articulation.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Trial the exact machine on every intended finish with the approved solution.
applicationFit.assessment: Trial the exact machine on every intended finish with the approved solution.
applicationFit.basis: Water, heat, brush action and chemistry can interact with floor finishes.
applicationFit.limitations: No universal floor compatibility is established.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Obtain written floor approval and inspect gloss, joints, residue and dry-back after a witnessed trial.
applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers limit use to stated surfaces and solutions.
applicationFit.scope: Exact floor construction, finish and model.

applicationFit.application: Mixed wet and dry household spills
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Use representative debris and record pickup, redeposition and recovery-tank handling.
applicationFit.assessment: Use representative debris and record pickup, redeposition and recovery-tank handling.
applicationFit.basis: Debris size, liquid viscosity, roller and separator design interact.
applicationFit.limitations: No claim covers every spill or hazardous material.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Exclude prohibited substances and run a controlled task trial.
applicationFit.evidence: Official sources position named machines for documented wet and dry household messes.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Evaluate the complete clean-store-return cycle, not only the floor pass.
applicationFit.assessment: Evaluate the complete clean-store-return cycle, not only the floor pass.
applicationFit.basis: Hair, organic residue and retained moisture increase roller, filter and tank maintenance.
applicationFit.limitations: Self-cleaning is model-specific and does not eliminate manual servicing.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Time tank emptying, roller removal, drying and odor-control work after each trial.
applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers document rinse, self-cleaning and removable service parts.

componentStack.role: Power the cordless drive, pump, roller and recovery systems.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources identify exact cordless energy arrangements.

componentStack.name: Clean-water and solution system
componentStack.role: Stores and meters approved cleaning liquid.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturer instructions distinguish water, formula and steam arrangements.

componentStack.name: Roller, scraper and floor head
componentStack.role: Agitate soil and control liquid at the floor interface.
componentStack.evidence: Official pages document different roller and head architectures.

componentStack.name: Recovery path and dirty-water tank
componentStack.role: Move and store recovered liquid and debris.
componentStack.evidence: Reviewed products identify separate dirty-water tanks and service components.

componentStack.name: Dock and cleaning cycle
componentStack.role: Charge, rinse or dry selected assemblies where provided.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturers publish model-specific dock and cleaning-cycle functions.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Surface approval, practical route time and residual moisture
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Ranking by runtime or tank size alone
procurementDecisions.assessment: Use a timed, measured trial on the actual route.
procurementDecisions.basis: The smaller tank, battery, soil load and maintenance stop can limit the route.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Catalogue values do not establish achieved productivity.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Record refill, emptying, recharge, dry-back and post-use service time.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm floor, solution, battery and charger approvals.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish model-specific runtime, tanks and surface limits.

procurementDecisions.intendedTask: Collect mixed wet and dry debris
procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Debris acceptance, separation and tank handling
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming all wet-dry labels permit the same material
procurementDecisions.assessment: Test only representative, manufacturer-approved non-hazardous messes.
procurementDecisions.basis: Head, suction path, strainer and float designs differ.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No page source authorizes hazardous or prohibited pickup.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain written exclusions and run a witnessed spill trial.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Inspect recovery seals, float and cleanup exposure.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturer pages describe different pickup and recovery systems.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Roller, filter, scraper, formula and battery availability
procurementDecisions.assessment: Price the complete consumables and service cycle.
procurementDecisions.basis: Wet systems retain moisture and use model-specific wear parts.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Attach five-year part numbers, prices and lead times to the quote.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm drying, dock ventilation and storage procedure.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official support sources identify model-specific service components.

engineeringChecks.reason: Leaks, overfill or incorrect orientation can affect electrical safety.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Inspect tank seals and follow filling, emptying, charging and storage instructions exactly.
engineeringChecks.evidence: IEC 60335-2-10 addresses safety of floor-treatment and wet-scrubbing machines while manuals define model procedures.
engineeringChecks.scope: Confirm regional conformity for the exact appliance.

engineeringChecks.reason: Moisture, heat, pH and roller action can damage finishes or leave residue.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain written approvals from both floor and equipment suppliers and perform a small-area trial.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer pages restrict surfaces and cleaning liquids.
engineeringChecks.scope: Exact floor finish, solution and model.

engineeringChecks.reason: Retained water and organic residue can affect odor and component condition.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Document tank, roller, filter, dock and drying steps with accountable frequencies.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources publish rinse, self-cleaning and removable-part maintenance.
engineeringChecks.scope: No medical or sterilization outcome is inferred.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-10:2021
standards.applicability: Particular safety requirements for covered floor-treatment machines and wet scrubbing machines.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the appliance and hazard scope.
standards.scope: Confirm exact product classification and regional adoption.

standards.name: Manufacturer surface and chemical instructions
standards.applicability: Defines permitted floors, liquids, debris, filling, charging, cleaning and storage for the purchased model.
standards.evidence: Reviewed official manuals and product pages provide model-specific boundaries.
standards.scope: Instructions are not interchangeable across brands or models.

developments.title: Current floor-washer systems continue to add dock and low-clearance functions
developments.summary: Reviewed current product families combine two-tank washing with model-specific self-cleaning, drying, edge or recline functions.
developments.evidence: Current official product and support pages document these functions without establishing cross-model equivalence.
developments.scope: Named products available or supported at verification time.
